subject: Timberline deal: exception request for per-tenant routing + telemetry export
thread_text:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Timberline deal: exception request for per-tenant routing + telemetry export

Team —

Quick background: Timberline Financial (prospect) is at final legal review but needs two things before they sign: (1) a per-tenant routing policy so they can route sensitive workloads to a dedicated routing lane (not full Dedicated capacity) and (2) a telemetry export that includes request/response trace metadata for compliance ingestion into their SIEM (they will ingest into Splunk). The deal is $1.2M ARR for year 1 with a two-year commit and is on the table contingent on these items.

I know both asks are outside our standard roadmap for Q3, but legal and procurement expect these as gating items. Can Product + Eng evaluate if we can: a) ship a scoped, feature-flagged per-tenant routing shim (routing policy + simple affinity rules) and b) provide a time-limited telemetry export (S3-delivered JSON with traceid, model, latency, top-level tokens) as a contractual deliverable?

Attachments: timberline-MAP-v2.xlsx (deal map), proposed-routing-schematic.png

High level constraints: Timberline requires a 6-week delivery from commitment, and wants the telemetry export retained for 90 days on their side. They asked for an architecture diagram and rollback plan.

Ask: Could Product triage scope and Eng/Platform give a rough feasibility + risk call today? If we can commit to a guarded, feature-flagged delivery and an ops playbook, Sales will push to sign by end of next week.

— Lukas
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Timberline deal: exception request for per-tenant routing + telemetry export

Thanks Lukas — important context. High-level thoughts after quick sync with Eng:

1) Per-tenant routing shim: feasible as a short-term shim if we implement a routing policy layer in the API gateway that annotates requests for a "Timberline" tenant and ensures they prefer a specific lane. Work items: policy config, routing table UI, tests. Risk: adds routing complexity and a surface area for misrouting if we don’t have strong assertion tests. Timeline: ~4–6 weeks for a gated rollout (feature flag + canary).

2) Telemetry export: we can produce a periodic S3 export with the fields you listed, but we need to confirm PII/token policy — we cannot include full prompt/response text without a data-processing agreement. We can include traceid, model_id, latency_ms, token_counts, and request metadata (route_id, tenant_id). Work items: export job, KMS consent, retention controls. Timeline: ~3–4 weeks for MVP.

Questions for Sales: 1) Does the customer require prompt/response bodies? 2) Is Timberline open to a scoped SLA exception limited to this tenant and time boxed? 3) Will this be added to the contract as a deliverable or a product feature for other customers?

If answers are favorable, PM can create an RFC + rollout plan today and schedule engineering scoping. CCing Laura for SE/implementation plan and Jasmine for CS/ops readiness.

— Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 12:26:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Timberline deal: exception request for per-tenant routing + telemetry export

Quick SE notes:
- The routing shim can be implemented at the ingress proxy layer with an additional tag and a simple affinity table. We can avoid changes to the serving runtime if we do it at the edge (preferred for speed).
- We'll need a canary policy so only Timberline traffic follows the new path until rollout. I can sketch the config and the edge rules.
- Telemetry export: recommend the S3 job with KMS-encrypted objects and an inventory manifest. We should add a manifest field for the export snapshot and a checksum.

Risks/ops:
- Operational burden: if we add tenant-specific routing there is an on-call runbook item for misrouted requests.
- Security/legal: if they ask for prompts/responses we'll need an explicit legal signoff + updated DPA.

I can produce a proposed config and a rollback playbook by EOD if PM/Eng want it for the RFC.

— Laura
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Timberline deal: exception request for per-tenant routing + telemetry export

Appreciate the quick triage. A few negotiation datapoints from Sales:
- Timberline has signaled willingness to add an enterprise onboarding credit (one-time) and a two-year revenue commitment if we can provide the two deliverables within 6 weeks.
- They prefer the telemetry to include request/response IDs and latency; they won't accept raw prompts.
- Legal wants the export to be delivered to their S3 and for us to provide a technical point of contact for the initial onboarding window.

From a commercial perspective, we can offer a 6-week technical delivery SLA, limited to this tenant, behind a feature flag. We'll also ask for a post-implementation review with a margin uplift in Y2.

Ben
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:48:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Timberline deal: exception request for per-tenant routing + telemetry export

Ops/CS checklist:
- We will require a temporary runbook for onboarding + rollback window (Laura to provide).
- Need clarity on who owns the export pipeline during the 90-day retention period on their side. If they manage the S3 bucket, we have to provide the schema and the initial support handshake.
- Monitoring: we should add an alert if export job fails for >2 consecutive runs and a guardrail to pause routing changes if any latency spike >25% from baseline is detected.

Also flagging that engineering will need a staging tenant to validate end-to-end. Please confirm Timberline agrees to a short staging window and sample data for validation (anonymized).

— Jasmine
Customer Success Lead
Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2026 17:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Timberline deal: exception request for per-tenant routing + telemetry export

OK — given answers from Sales and SE, we'll proceed with a scoped RFC:
- Scope: routing shim at ingress proxy + S3 telemetry export (no prompt/response payloads).
- Delivery plan: 5-week sprint to deliver feature-flagged routing + 3-week parallel work for export job; engineering will prioritize routing first and create the canary. Target ship date: 2026-09-16 (feature-flag on Timberline tenant).
- Rollout: canary -> 1% -> 10% -> full on tenant. Rollback plan included in RFC.
- Requirements: Timberline signs Addendum confirming no raw prompt exchange and agrees to provide staging tenant/access for validation.

I'll open the RFC in the product board and tag Eng; Laura, please attach the config diagram and rollback playbook. Jasmine, please draft the onboarding runbook template. Lukas/Ben: please secure the legal addendum and confirm drive link for S3 destination.

I'll post the RFC link here once created.

— Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
